landing.title: TS-Lens
landing.s0_title:
You know the pattern,
but have no example
landing.s0_desc: In time-series analysis such as energy monitoring, equipment diagnostics, and anomaly detection, users often know the concept of the pattern they want, but have no representative segment to use for search.
landing.s1_desc: Query-by-Example needs an example, Sketch-based requires manual drawing, and Language-based needs paired training data. We need a way to search right away without any example.
landing.s2_desc: TS-Lens lets you express and search for patterns in many ways — natural language, sketches, and more — without task-specific training. Search results expose the query waveform and its generation provenance, and results accumulate through a human-in-the-loop process.
landing.s3_desc: When a user describes a pattern, a rule-based pre-pass and the selected model (local or external LLM) generate a normalized query waveform, which is used to search for similar intervals. Results are accumulated into label baskets and presets.
landing.s4_desc: Natural language Text, freehand Sketch, range Select, sample card Sample, predefined Preset, and cluster representative Cluster. Every input is unified into the same Query Shape.
landing.s5_title:
Inspect the query used
alongside the results
landing.s5_desc: The Text result's Query card shows the generated waveform and the actual engine, model, and fallback provenance. If it differs from your intent, revise the description and search again; the query used for retrieval is not hidden.
landing.s6_title:
Review search results
and build pattern knowledge
landing.s6_desc: Analysts review results and label them directly. Meaningful patterns are collected in the Label Basket, frequently used queries are saved as Custom Presets, and final results are Exported.
landing.s1_fig_gap_line1: Users know the target pattern concept,
landing.s1_fig_gap_line2: but lack a representative segment for retrieval.
landing.s5_fig_msg1: See the query used for every search

finder.title: TS-Lens — Pattern Finder
finder.ds_info_desc: Select a dataset stored in DB and choose columns to analyze.
finder.ds_info_single: Single — Continuous time series, sliding window search
finder.ds_info_collection: Collection — Same-length segment collection, segment comparison
finder.ds_info_multi: Selecting multiple columns enables overlay display + multi-column similarity calculation
finder.chart_select_desc: Drag over the main chart to choose the shape you want to find.
finder.chart_select_region: Box-select the desired range on the time-series chart
finder.chart_select_query: The selected segment becomes the search query shape
finder.chart_select_length: Enable Fixed Length to keep the search window size constant
finder.chart_select_hint: Drag on the chart to select a query segment
finder.draw_tip_sketch: Use mouse or touch to sketch the shape you're looking for
finder.draw_tip_shape: A rough sketch is enough — it will be normalized automatically
finder.draw_tip_search: Find similar segments in the time series matching your drawn pattern
finder.fixed_length_desc: Use a predefined window size instead of drag length.
finder.fixed_on: ON — Search with fixed window size
finder.fixed_off: OFF — Use the actual dragged length on the chart
finder.fixed_preset: Choose time preset or enter custom point count
finder.start_mode_desc: Determines how search windows are positioned.
finder.calendar_desc: Aligns to calendar boundaries (00:00, Monday, etc). Stride auto-set to window size for non-overlapping search.
finder.free_desc: Search all positions at stride intervals. Overlapping windows possible.
finder.free_example: e.g., stride=1 checks every position, stride=window for no overlap
finder.window_size_desc: Sliding window length for search. Choose time preset or enter custom.
finder.stride_desc: Search window step size (number of points).
finder.stride_1: 1 — Compare at every position (most precise, slow)
finder.stride_big: Large value — Faster but may miss optimal matches
finder.stride_auto: Auto-set to window size in Calendar Align mode
finder.sample_hint: Click a segment card to select as query
finder.sample_desc: Select a segment card as the query and find similar segments by shape comparison.
finder.sample_click: Click any segment card to set it as the query
finder.sample_multi: Multi-column: per-column distances are equally averaged into one similarity score
finder.sample_sort: Results can be sorted by similarity or date
finder.preset_desc: Search using built-in or custom reference shapes.
finder.preset_shapes: 7 built-in shapes: rise, fall, flat, bell, spike, V-shape, dip
finder.preset_custom: Custom presets can be saved from cluster centroids
finder.preset_classify: "All" classifies every segment against all preset shapes at once
finder.text_search_desc: Describe a shape in natural language. Explicit shape terms are generated immediately; only compound descriptions use the LLM.
finder.text_example: e.g. "sharp drop followed by gradual recovery"
finder.text_meta: Setting metadata (column name, unit) improves accuracy
finder.text_preview: Generated pattern and model provenance appear in the result Query card
finder.text_seg_mode: Segment mode: LLM generates a shape matching segment length for direct comparison
finder.text_placeholder: e.g. sharp drop then gradual recovery / bell-shaped solar power
finder.compare_desc: Method for measuring similarity between query and data segments.
finder.cosine_desc: Compare direction/shape only, ignores magnitude difference
finder.dtw_desc: Allows time-axis warping, can compare different lengths
finder.shape_desc: Feature-based comparison (std, slope, peaks) — best for preset classification
finder.zscore_desc: Normalize to mean=0, std=1 before comparison.
finder.zscore_on: ON — Compare shape only (50kW and 100kW match if same pattern)
finder.zscore_off: OFF — Absolute value differences also matter
finder.result_filter_desc: Limit the number of search results.
finder.topk_desc: Show only top N results by similarity
finder.nms_desc: Keeps only the best match among overlapping results. With small stride, hundreds of nearly identical matches may be found at similar positions — NMS keeps only the highest similarity one and removes the rest. Thus, actual results may be fewer than Top-K.
finder.nan_desc: How to handle NaN (missing values) during comparison.
finder.nan_interp_method: Interpolate — Fill with surrounding values or foundation model
finder.nan_max_ratio: Max missing ratio — Auto-exclude segments exceeding ratio
finder.nan_skip_hint: Segments exceeding this ratio are automatically skipped
finder.verbalts_note: VerbalTS experiment · English input · generates 128 points, then resamples to the search length. Try an example below.
finder.text_to_ts_note: Rule pre-pass → local model or external LLM · explicit shape terms are generated instantly without a model
finder.model_ready: {0} connected · AI handles complex text; rules handle explicit shapes
finder.model_limited: {0} is offline · explicit shape terms still work through rules
finder.chart_select: Select mode: Drag to define query range
finder.chart_zoom: Zoom mode: Drag to select zoom area
finder.chart_pan: Pan mode: Drag to move chart
finder.sketch_window_popup: Set how many points the sketch pattern corresponds to in the actual data.
finder.mc_note_full: Combined Search: selected columns are scored together in one search
finder.mc_note_primary: Per-Column Classification: Shapes › All analyzes each column separately and shows tabs
finder.chart_footer: Drag in Select mode to define query · Explore in Zoom/Pan mode · Scroll to zoom
finder.seg_mode_desc: Display same-length segments as individual cards.
finder.seg_click: Click card → Select as query segment
finder.seg_search: Search → 1:1 similarity comparison with remaining segments (multi-column support)
finder.seg_concat: Full view → Concatenate segments into continuous time series
finder.seg_hint: Click a card to select as query
finder.split_desc: Split continuous data into segments of specified length.
finder.discovery_no_selection: Select a dataset and column in Finder first, then run auto discovery.
finder.discovery_normalize_hint: On: strip each segment's mean and spread so only the shape is compared. Off: keep magnitude and bias, which suits data like forecast error where 'how much, in which direction' is the point.
finder.discovery_portfolio_sub: Ranked regimes with representative shapes and example windows.
finder.discovery_portfolio_placeholder: Run discovery to build a pattern portfolio.
finder.discovery_notice_unit_refined: Unit auto-adjusted to {0} to ensure enough segments.
finder.discovery_notice_seg_cap: Only {0} segments, so clusters are capped at {1}. Choose a finer segment unit or use a longer time range for finer patterns.
finder.discovery_notice_interpret_degraded: The interpretation pass rejected every pattern, so the clustering result is shown as-is. Labels and descriptions may be unreliable.
finder.discovery_col_none: No column analysis for this pattern.
finder.discovery_col_insight: {0} most distinguishes the patterns ({1} discriminative power).
finder.discovery_matrix_none: No analysis data for the matrix.
finder.discovery_no_portfolio: No stable pattern portfolio was found.
finder.discovery_found_none: No additional similar segments were found.
finder.discovery_subdivide_min: At least 6 segments are required to subdivide.
finder.discovery_subdivide_none: This pattern cannot be subdivided further.
finder.discovery_handoff_toast: Ready to search segments with the "{0}" pattern from Discovery.
finder.discovery_handoff_failed: Could not hand the pattern to Finder. Pick it from Shapes instead.
finder.discovery_seg_too_short: The chosen time unit yields segments of only {0} point(s); at least {1} are required. Pick a longer unit.
finder.cpu_ready: CPU basic mode · no additional model required
finder.cpu_note: Uses rule-based shapes and statistical descriptions. Complex text requires a model or a sketch.

data.title: TS-Lens — DB Data Management
data.upload_info_desc: Stores time-series CSVs in the DB. Encoding, delimiter and the base column are auto-detected and can be changed in the preview before saving.
data.upload_folder: store each file as its own source (individual) or merge all files in time order (merge). Files for different sites or regions go in as individual
data.upload_auto: Base column (time/index) is auto-detected and can be manually changed
data.upload_meta_opt: Metadata is optional. Column min/max are physical bounds used by preprocessing as out-of-range filters. Each field has an ⓘ explanation
data.drag_csv: Drag a CSV file or click to select
data.drag_folder: Drag a folder or click to select
data.folder_hint: Automatically detects CSV files in folder
data.merge_desc: Merges all CSVs in time order into a single source. Only for one site whose period is split across files.
data.ds_list_desc: All datasets stored in the DB. Open a card for sources, columns and a preview; use Settings to edit column descriptions and allowed ranges.
data.ds_auto_detect: Metadata and sampling interval are auto-detected
data.empty_dataset_hint: Open the Data Upload tab to import a CSV
data.del_warn_files: Original files are deleted too. This cannot be undone.
data.del_warn_nofile: No original file is stored for this dataset — it cannot be re-imported from the app after deletion.
data.models_desc: Models used for text→time series and time series→text. Admins connect external LLMs here.
data.ext_desc: Connects Anthropic (Claude) or an OpenAI-compatible server. The key is stored in a server file only; the UI shows its last four characters. When enabled, it appears as a model choice for the ticked tasks (text→shape, series→text, upload metadata inference). Usage is logged in tokens, monthly cost is estimated, and a warning and a limit apply. The provider console remains the source of truth for billing.
data.ext_remove_confirm: This deletes the external LLM connection and its stored key. Continue?
data.ext_off_note: Off — not offered as a model choice
data.local_desc: Models served from this host, managed by config files (config/model/text_ts.yaml, runtime.yaml). The default series→text model ChatTS-14B is loaded onto the GPU on demand and unloaded after 5 idle minutes, so the first call takes about 2 minutes and later calls about 20 seconds. Click a header to sort.
data.ai_infer_done: Filled from AI — review, edit, then save ({0}, confidence {1})
data.ext_usage_blocked: Monthly limit (${0}) reached — external LLM calls are blocked
data.ext_usage_note: Estimated from token counts. The Anthropic Console bill is authoritative; set a limit there too.
data.ai_infer_auto: AI is inferring metadata… (fields stay editable)
data.ai_status_off: External LLM off — enable it in Models and tick "upload metadata inference" to infer automatically
data.ai_status_done: {0} replied · {1}s · fields filled — review, edit, then save
data.ai_status_ready: {0} ready — upload a file to infer automatically
data.ai_filled_legend: Red border = filled by AI (editing clears it)
data.ai_use_toggle: AI metadata inference for this upload
data.ai_status_skipped: AI inference skipped for this upload — turn on to infer from the uploaded file now
data.mi_key: Identifier that never changes after saving. Lowercase ascii, digits and underscores only; used verbatim in API paths and file paths. e.g. elia_offshore_wind_hourly
data.mi_name: Name shown in lists and chart titles. One line: what, where, at which resolution.
data.mi_base: Column that orders the rows. A timestamp column gives a time axis; a sequence number gives an evenly spaced index. Duplicate timestamps follow the selected policy.
data.mi_desc: Source, collection method, period and caveats in 1–2 sentences. Used verbatim in search and in the ts_to_text prompt.
data.mi_location: Measurement site or region (e.g. Belgian North Sea offshore, Jeju Haengwon). Groups datasets from the same place for comparison.
data.mi_facility: Type of equipment measured (e.g. offshore wind farm, PV inverter, met mast). Drives domain-specific preprocessing defaults.
data.mi_capacity: Rated capacity (e.g. 2,262 MW, 100 kW). Reference for normalising generation to capacity factor.
data.mi_interval: Time step between rows (e.g. 1 hour, 15 min). A value typed here overrides the step detected from the file.
data.mi_chars: Properties to know before analysis: seasonality, gaps, unit changes, meaning of negatives. Shown as a note when reading anomaly results.
data.mi_tags: Domain, period and purpose classification. Used for list filters and similar-dataset suggestions; several may be selected.
data.mi_col_label: Display name shown in charts and tables. The original column name stays unchanged.
data.mi_col_unit: Physical unit (MW, °C, %, m/s). Attached to axis labels and descriptions; only same-unit columns are overlaid.
data.mi_col_desc: One sentence on what the column means. For forecasts, the issue time; for measurements, average vs instantaneous.
data.mi_col_min: Physical lower bound a correct sensor could report. Values below it are flagged/removed as out-of-range in preprocessing. Not the sample minimum.
data.mi_col_max: Physical upper bound (e.g. generation ≤ capacity, humidity ≤ 100). Empty disables the upper check.
data.ai_status_ask: {0} ready — turn on the switch to let AI infer metadata for the uploaded file (nothing is queried until then)
data.upload_dup: Duplicate timestamps follow the chosen policy (reject, first, last, mean, shift). When every timestamp appears exactly k times, the upload is diagnosed as k files merged together
data.upload_ai: AI metadata inference: the switch at the top of the card lets the connected external LLM fill key, name, description, location, facility, capacity, interval, characteristics, tags and column label/unit/description/min/max. AI-filled fields get a red border that clears when edited. Off by default; the last choice is remembered
data.ds_delete: Deleting removes linked preprocessing results, labels, baskets, presets, caches and source files, and creates a DB backup first. The dataset key must be typed to confirm
data.individual_desc: Stores each CSV as its own source (collection dataset). Use this for files from different sites or regions.

preprocess.title: TS-Lens — Preprocessing
preprocess.pipeline_order: Executed in order: Extreme values → Time gap fill → NaN imputation. Adaptive method: short gaps use linear, medium gaps use MOMENT FM, very long gaps are skipped.
preprocess.step1_desc: Choose value range limit or outlier clamping to handle extreme values
preprocess.step2_desc: Check time gaps between data points and insert NaN for missing timestamps
preprocess.step2_detail: NaN is inserted for missing timestamps; actual interpolation is handled in the next step.
preprocess.step3_desc: Fill NaN values using adaptive method (short gaps: linear, medium gaps: MOMENT FM, long gaps: skip)
preprocess.empty: Select a dataset to run diagnostics and preprocessing.
preprocess.desc_missing: Estimated from gaps against the sampling interval
preprocess.desc_oor: Values outside the configured range (physical bounds)

basket.title: Label Basket
basket.subtitle: Review captured patterns, attach clear labels, and export a trustworthy dataset.
basket.chart_scale_note: Each column is scaled independently to compare shape; line height does not show absolute magnitude.
